system: You fill a typed JSON schema for ONE piece of public feedback. You never recommend funds or stocks. Evidence spans must be copied character-for-character from the text. Output JSON only.
prompt:
Code this playstore text about SIPs (systematic investment plans in mutual funds).

CODEBOOK (use only these theme_id values, or "other"):
- payment_autopay_failure [stop]: Autopay / mandate / payment failures. Instalments are missed, fail or are debited wrongly because of autopay, mandate, bank or payment problems, or because there is no auto-debit and the investor must pay manually each month. Include: Autopay or mandate not working, mandate setup failing, manual monthly payment burden, missed instalments despite balance, double debits, bounce or ACH charges. (Missing reminders or forgetting to pay go to missed_reminders_forgetting.) Exclude: App crashes unrelated to payments (app_reliability_errors); deliberate cancellation.
- missing_sip_controls [stop]: Can't pause, skip, reduce or cancel easily. The investor wants to pause, skip, change the amount or date, or cancel, but the option is missing, broken or deliberately hard, so they cancel outright or feel trapped. Include: No pause/skip/edit/step-up control, can't reduce amount, cancellation hidden or blocked, cancel flows full of upsell screens. Exclude: Payment failures (payment_autopay_failure).
- app_reliability_errors [stop]: App bugs, slow processing and confusing status. SIP orders stay in processing, units are allotted late, the app crashes or an update breaks flows, or the investor cannot tell whether a SIP is active or where money went after cancelling. Include: Orders stuck processing, late allotment, app down or crashing, SIP vanished, money not returned after cancel, autopay still showing after cancel. (Problems caused specifically by a redesign or update go to disruptive_app_updates.) Exclude: Payment-rail failures (payment_autopay_failure).
- fees_paywall [stop]: New fees, paywalls and upselling. The platform starts charging for basics, locks features behind subscriptions or pushes paid plans, and the investor stops or moves SIPs. Include: Subscription or premium paywalls, charges for statements or tracking, aggressive upselling, hidden charges. Exclude: Fund expense ratios or commissions in regular plans (switching_plan_or_platform).
- support_trust_breakdown [stop]: Unresponsive support and loss of trust. Problems go unresolved because support or the agent does not respond, and the investor loses trust in the platform. Include: Tickets ignored, no customer care, agent unreachable, 'fraud' or 'scam' language after unresolved issues. Exclude: The underlying technical issue itself (code that theme too).
- returns_disappointment [stop]: Disappointing returns or market fear. Flat, negative or below-expectation returns over months or years, or fear during market falls, lead the investor to stop or consider stopping. Include: No returns after N years, losses, worse than FD, panic in falls, 'thinking of stopping'. Exclude: Expectations stated at the start without an outcome (return_expectations).
- cash_need_affordability [stop]: Cash need or amount too high. The investor needs the money elsewhere, or the SIP amount (or step-up) becomes hard to sustain. Include: Urgent money need, job or income loss, house or EMI, step-up outpacing salary, saving everything into the SIP. Exclude: Planned goal completion; lock-in ending.
- platform_or_fund_initiated [stop]: Stopped or changed by the platform or fund. The SIP was paused, deleted or cancelled by the fund house or platform rather than by the investor. Include: Fund suspensions, SIPs deleted after rule changes, platform cancelling inactive SIPs. Exclude: Investor-chosen stops.
- switching_plan_or_platform [stop]: Switching plan, fund or platform (not a real drop). The investor stops a SIP only to restart it elsewhere, e.g. regular to direct, a different fund or another app. Include: Regular to direct, moving SIPs to another app, changing funds. Exclude: Leaving SIP investing altogether.
- early_confusion_first_months [behaviour]: Early confusion after the first instalment. In the first weeks or months after starting, the investor misunderstands how the SIP works (when instalments are taken, where the money is, what cancelling or redeeming does) and stops or cancels as a result. Include: Confusion about the next instalment date, cancelling within days or weeks of starting, accidental cancellation, not knowing whether the SIP is active, a first SIP that started but was not properly understood (e.g. via an agent). Exclude: Barriers before the first investment (minimum or initial amount, KYC, account opening) - out of scope because the focus is investors who have started. Long-running SIPs (other themes).
- return_expectations [start]: Specific return expectations at the start. Starts with a concrete expectation of returns or a corpus (e.g. 12% a year, 1 crore in 10 years), often set by ads or creators. Include: Stated % returns, crore targets, 'become rich', expectations from videos. Exclude: Long-term motives without numbers (long_term_discipline).
- missed_reminders_forgetting [stop]: No reminders, so instalments are forgotten. Instalments are missed because the app sends no reminder or due-date notification, and the investor forgets to pay or place the order. Include: No SIP reminders or notifications, forgetting manual payments, missing several dates in a row. Exclude: Autopay failing when it was set up (payment_autopay_failure).
- disruptive_app_updates [stop]: App updates that break or hide SIP flows. A redesign or update removes or hides SIP features (pay button, SIP list, modify, tracking), so the investor misses payments, cannot manage SIPs or decides to leave. Include: Complaints that start with 'after the latest update' about SIP payment, visibility or management; old version was better. Exclude: Bugs not tied to an update (app_reliability_errors); paywalls introduced with an update (code fees_paywall too).
- charges_lockin_surprise [stop]: Surprise charges, lock-ins or tax at exit. The investor is surprised by exit loads, lock-in periods, tax or other charges when stopping or redeeming, and feels misled. Include: Exit loads not explained, ELSS lock-in surprises, unexpected tax or fees at redemption. Exclude: Platform subscription fees (fees_paywall).
- conflicting_advice [behaviour]: Conflicting or misleading advice. The investor is confused or loses confidence because creators, agents or ads give conflicting or misleading messages about SIPs, or they were mis-sold (e.g. a regular plan without understanding it). Include: Some sources say do SIP and others say don't; feeling misled by creators or agents; discovering commissions later. Exclude: Their own disappointment with returns (returns_disappointment).
- long_term_discipline [behaviour]: Long-term discipline (protective). Investor keeps going because of a long horizon, a family goal, discipline or experience of holding through falls. Include: Multi-decade horizons, family or retirement goals, holding through losses, set-and-forget, increasing over time. Exclude: Statements of intent from people who have not started.

Return one JSON object:
{
 "record_id": "playstore_f3f2b0069ed3",
 "source": "playstore",
 "sip_status": "stopped" | "paused" | "reduced" | "continuing" | "unclear",   // the WRITER's own SIP status as stated
 "sip_status_evidence": "<verbatim quote showing the status, or null if unclear>",
 "first_time_investor": "yes" | "no" | "unclear",                // only "yes"/"no" if the text says so
 "first_time_evidence": "<verbatim quote, or null if unclear>",
 "time_since_start": "<1m" | "1-6m" | "6-12m" | ">12m" | "unclear",   // how long the writer has had the SIP, if stated
 "time_since_start_evidence": "<verbatim quote, or null if unclear>",
 "themes": [{"theme_id": "...", "evidence_span": "<verbatim quote>", "severity": 1|2|3, "confidence": 0.0-1.0}],
 "one_line_reason": "<why they stopped/paused/continued, max 20 words, or null>"
}
Rules:
- stopped = cancelled/ended (or clearly says "I want to stop my SIP"); paused = paused/skipped/missed instalments but keeping it; reduced = lowered the amount; continuing = still investing. A question like "should I stop?" is unclear.
- Themes answer three questions: why they started and what they expected (start), how their behaviour changed after starting (behaviour), what led them to pause/reduce/stop (stop). Code only themes the text actually supports.
- severity: 1 = minor mention, 2 = clear reason or friction, 3 = decisive reason / strong distress.
- Every evidence quote must be an exact substring of the text (you may shorten it, never reword or translate it).
